stem:
In mammals, arteries branch to form smaller blood vessels called arterioles.

Arterioles branch to form capillaries that supply blood to tissues.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain the ways in which the structure of an artery is adapted to its function.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Fig. 4.1 shows transmission electron micrographs of cross-sections through an arteriole and a capillary.

{{figure:figure_4_1.png}}

arteriole magnification $\times 2000$ capillary magnification $\times 6500$

Fig. 4.1

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Identify the cells inside the lumen of the arteriole in Fig. 4.1 **and** state **one** reason for your identification.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the differences between the arteriole and the capillary that are **visible** in Fig. 4.1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Fig. 4.2 shows a capillary network in a mammalian tissue.

The arrows indicate the direction of flow of body fluids.

{{figure:figure_4_2.png}}

Fig. 4.2

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Capillaries have a role in the formation of tissue fluid.

Explain how tissue fluid is formed in the capillary network.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The vessels labelled **X** in Fig. 4.2 carry excess tissue fluid back into the circulatory system.

Name the fluid inside the vessels labelled **X** **and** state **one** way in which its composition differs from blood plasma.
